newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Cambodia should keep two-party coalition - Manila.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia should keep two-party coalition - Manila.

text.p: The Philippines said on Tuesday that Cambodia must maintain its two-party ruling coalition, and hinted that continued fighting could prevent Phnom Penh from joining the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) this month.
Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon said the issue of Cambodia's membership in ASEAN would be reviewed by the group's foreign ministers at their special meeting in Kuala Lumpur on Thursday.

ASEAN has agreed to accept Cambodia, Burma and Laos as new members on July 23, but diplomats said the outbreak of fighting in Phnom Penh between the forces of that country's two prime ministers might have endangered Cambodia's membership.
Siazon told reporters he did not think the membership of Burma and Laos would be affected by the upheaval in Cambodia.
"This (Cambodia) is a case of force majeure... Why should you punish the other two?" he said.
Siazon said the establishment of a two-party coalition led by First Prime Minister Norodom Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen was an international commitment by Cambodia.
"I think Hun Sen knows that he needs a coalition," Siazon said, adding this was the reason Hun Sen was now negotiating with Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party.

"Otherwise, what will happen is they will quarrel, they will be shooting each other," Siazon said. "So that means they can't comply with AFTA (ASEAN Free Trade Area) requirements. How can you comply with the requirements if you are shooting each other?"

Asked if preserving the coalition between FUNCINPEC and Hun Sen's Cambodian People's Party was now impossible, Siazon said: "In politics, nothing is impossible... We are hoping that (they) will still be able to find a formula."

The situation is bad in the sense that the first prime minister has already announced that he will fight it out," Siazon he added. "Some of his generals are out in the countryside and probably are trying to regroup."
ASEAN was at the forefront of a series of peace talks which led to an accord in 1991 among the warring Cambodian factions.
